patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches include a clearly drawn text input near the top of the page in a search area; on mobile it spans most of the width, and on desktop it appears as a smaller search box aligned to the right of the guide/tag area.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Search should at minimum support typing and submit behavior; depending on implementation it may also support enter-to-submit and optional live suggestions/results. Focus styling and keyboard submission are implied.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not show whether results appear live, on a separate results page, or via autocomplete dropdown.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The explicit search input field implies a form submission flow that needs input handling, even if the field may be optional.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Validate/sanitize the search query before submit, handle empty submissions gracefully, and provide focus/error feedback if submission rules exist.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No required marker or error state is drawn, so strict validation may be minimal.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a long vertical feed of repeated content cards followed by a grouped set of multiple 'btn' controls near the bottom, suggesting pagination or a manual reveal of more content sections/items.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A button may load additional cards/articles into the feed or paginate to more results. Loading state and appended content handling would be needed if implemented dynamically.
patterns_found.ambiguities: Those bottom buttons could also be simple navigation/footer links rather than a true load-more control; the sketch does not label them.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a mostly content-driven article page with relatively light JavaScript needs. Across both viewports, the only clearly required interactive behavior is the search form. Mobile additionally suggests a long stacked feed with possible progressive loading or pagination controls near the bottom, while desktop appears more fully expanded with side content visible at once and no strong evidence of hidden navigation, tabs, accordions, or modal behavior.
